subject.title: [Feature]: Multi-role support in Chat UI for multi-agent workflows

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable per-message sender identity contract for multi-agent conversations, and which canonical fields and trust rules should flow through Gateway schemas, transcripts, live/history events, and Control UI rendering?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but the permanent fix defines a cross-surface protocol and persistence contract rather than a narrow renderer bug; automation should not choose field names, trust semantics, or compatibility behavior alone.

options.title: Add Durable Sender Identity
options.body: Adopt an additive sender object with id, kind, display name, source session or agent, and render metadata, then migrate the affected protocol, transcript, event, and UI paths together.

options.title: Keep SenderLabel Projection Only
options.body: Treat current `senderLabel`/provenance display as the intended scope and leave only narrower bugs such as requester names or blank labels to separate issues.

options.title: Defer To Narrow Bugs
options.body: Keep this broad issue paused while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/38570 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/92327 handle the immediate known gaps, accepting that durable audit identity remains unowned.

recommendation.title: Add Durable Sender Identity
recommendation.body: Adopt an additive sender object with id, kind, display name, source session or agent, and render metadata, then migrate the affected protocol, transcript, event, and UI paths together.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is around inter-session provenance, protocol-adjacent session work, and prior review of this exact product/API boundary.
